Pre-1962 material can help identify passage families; it cannot certify 1962 text or wording.

researchNotes: The nine online incipits are candidates, not certified transcriptions of the 1962 Missale Romanum. Keep exactSourceLocator null, all three language verification flags false, and publicationAllowed false until original Missal page/section collation is completed.
Read only the nine Proper components from secondary pages; generic preparation, Ordinary, Gloria and Credo shown elsewhere on those pages must not be inherited as processional Mass content.
No English translation was approved for the Secret in the sampled Missale Online witness. Check all English and French renderings independently and retain their provenance and re-use permissions.
The 1960 general rubrics (especially 80-90, 346-347) govern the class and processional condition, independently of the secondary text source.
No change to live Mass selection or Calendar ownership.

Treat the explicit service as PUBLIC_PROCESSION or ORDINARY_AUTHORIZED_SUPPLICATIONS. Do not enable the conditional Mass on private prayer or date alone; a I-class day impedes the II-class votive (1960 §§341, 346–347).

The 1962 original printed heading begins on page 341; original source index independently confirms Introit/Collect/Epistle there, but per-section leaf collation remains pending and no latinVerified flags have been lifted.
The current test example dated 2027-05-10 was after Ascension and was replaced by 2027-05-03 for the representative Rogations Monday.

Substantive correction: earlier online candidate 'Confitemini Domino' as Rogation Alleluia was inappropriate. The original 1962 Missal's Eastertide paired Alleluia uses Ps 78:9-10 (Propitius esto) and Ps 30:8 (Exsultabo et laetabor).
Substantive correction: Communion antiphon in the Missale Romanum 1962 is explicitly cited to Lc 11:9-10, not Matthew 7:7-8, although words occur in both.

Nine Latin source-research strings with newly drafted English and French translations recorded separately in data/mass/rogation-proper-trilingual.v1.json. Page-image proofing, liturgical editorial approval, public-service runtime selection and mobile reader tests remain pending.

Latin strings are unaccented normalized transcriptions; not literal typographical facsimiles.

The original OCR mirror uses pp.341–342 while the separate Vatican typical edition photographed on Gregobase uses pp.347–349. All source locators now cite the specific Vatican scan, preventing false page-number agreement.

The Mass-source proper's original English/French translations remain drafts and source gate stays closed. The 1962 Missal also provides outside-Eastertide Gradual, Alleluia and Tract variants; they are captured as unpublished research-only alternatives.
